title: LLMOps run manifest
description: Single source of truth for one pipeline run, stored at s3://<bucket>/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json. start_pipeline seeds it (seed_manifest); agents read it first and write their own entries into `stages`; the harness driver verifies a stage's claims before recording them in `stage_history`, `attestations` and `escalations`. The schema describes what those writers actually emit -- tests/test_manifest_schema.py validates seed_manifest's output and the driver's records against it -- so a field that drifts fails a test instead of the schema quietly describing a manifest nobody writes. The iteration counter drives the remediation loop (max 3).

run_id.description: run-<UTC %Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ>-<8 hex chars>, minted by start_pipeline.new_run_id. Three manifests written by hand before start_pipeline existed carry other ids; nothing mints that form today.

trigger_source.description: Free-form label of whoever started the run, taken verbatim from the start_pipeline event (default `unknown`). A pattern rather than an enum because the callers name themselves: in code today conductor, webhook, console, scheduler, resurrector-schedule, github-actions, protocol-probe; in live manifests also hand-named relaunches and rehearsals. tests/test_manifest_schema.py checks every literal the repo passes.

params.description: DEFAULT_PARAMS < trigger params < signed plan, merged by start_pipeline. Immutable after seeding (IMMUTABLE_MANIFEST_KEYS).

plan.description: Run plan written by the llmops_orchestrator conductor (plan.json contents): per-stage params, cost estimate, quality bar. Empty object when the run has no plan.

approval.description: The signed human-acceptance record, stored verbatim. Empty object for non-conductor runs.

iteration.description: Remediation-loop counter; 0 on first attempt, incremented per finetune remediate cycle, escalates to human when it would exceed 3

stages.description: SHARED and AGENT-WRITABLE, so not a verified record. The driver writes the bare stage name (data-prep, finetune, eval, deploy, monitor) with status `completed` when it accepts a stage_complete; agents write entries of their own -- often keyed `<stage>.<task>` or `<stage>.<task>.i<n>`, sometimes over the bare name -- in a vocabulary of their own (live: complete, in_progress, launched, blocked, escalated_conflict, ...), with `outputs` and `evidence` sometimes objects, and a few entries are lists. Only the driver's own entries are normalized (report.normalize_stage_complete: outputs a list of S3 URIs each verified to exist, metrics an object, evidence a string), so no field but `status` is typed here: normalize before reading, or read `stage_history`, which only the driver writes.

stage_history.description: Append-only, driver-written: one record per accepted stage_complete, re-read from S3 before each append so no iteration overwrites another's.

outputs.description: S3 URIs of produced artifacts, each verified to exist by the driver. Empty array is VALID (empty-but-valid is distinct from missing).

evidence.description: The stage's one-paragraph proof of what was verified

attestations.description: Append-only, driver-written: what the DRIVER measured about a stage's claim, as opposed to what the stage said. kind `judge_instrument` compares a claimed judge-prompt digest with the canonical object's bytes. kind `gold_extract` (Phase 1 PR-08) re-reads a training extract under s3://<DATA_BUCKET>/lakehouse/extracts/ and recomputes its sha256 and line count; any other URI is refused, not fetched. `verified` is false, with `error`, when the object could not be read or the claim was refused.

uri.description: gold_extract: the extract the stage claimed

computed_sha256.description: gold_extract: the digest the driver computed

snapshot_id.description: gold_extract: the Gold snapshot the stage claims the extract was taken at

escalations.description: Append-only, driver-written by handle_escalate for an escalation that belongs to this run.

lakehouse.description: The lakehouse dataset this run builds (lakehouse_ingest: named after the run, with the generator's seed and scale) or trains on (lakehouse: params.lakehouse_dataset); null in every other mode (start_pipeline.lakehouse_input). Written at seeding because the Glue states write nothing to the manifest, and it is the same object the state machine formats the jobs' arguments from.

models.description: The resolved record of model CONSENT: role -> model id, signed plan > trigger params > DEFAULT_MODELS (start_pipeline._resolve_models). Immutable after seeding. Where an open-weight model came from (hf_repo, revision, ...) is plan content, not a role, and is not copied here.

teacher.description: e.g. us.deepseek.r1-v1:0 or a signed plan's teacher
